_comment: granite5_ctc (Granite Speech 5.0 TurboCTC) tolerances. Stage 4 finalized.
Correctness regime (every number below was measured in exactly this one):
GGUF:          granite-speech-5.0-470m-turboctc-BF16.gguf, the reference
tier — BF16 weights, F32 norms/biases/BN stats, F16 conv
kernels (gguf_common.reference_dtype_for).
KV cache:      none. encoder-ctc is a single forward with no decoder
loop, so --kv-type does not reach a graph.
Frontend:      the production C++ path (MelFrontend per_utterance +
host deltas + 2-frame stacking). No reference-mel
injection is used anywhere in this file. `mel.in` is a
real frontend-parity gate, not a pinned read.
Backend:       CPU, --threads 1 (scripts/validate.py defaults).
Reference:     transformers 5.17.0 GraniteSpeech5ForCTC at F32
(oracle_dtype in the golden manifest), eager attention.
Cases:         jfk (1100 mel frames, even) and dots (3533, odd); each
entry takes the max over both.
Dominant drift source: ggml's BF16 matmul rounds the F32 activation to
BF16 before the dot product, so the C++ computes BF16 x BF16 against an
F32 x F32 reference. This is NOT weight rounding: the BF16 and F32 GGUFs
built from this checkpoint hold numerically identical weights (max diff
2.98e-08 across all 520 tensors, and that residue is the F16-vs-F32 conv
kernel bucket, not the BF16 bucket, which round-trips exactly). BF16
carries 8 mantissa bits, so one rounding is ~2^-9 = 0.2% relative; the
observed 0.3%-1.6% of p99_abs is that compounding over 16 blocks.
Control measurement that localizes it (Stage 4, not a shipped artifact):
the same C++ graph against an F32-tier GGUF of the same checkpoint
(scripts/convert-granite5_ctc.py --reference-dtype f32) matches the F32
oracle to 3e-6..5e-5 RELATIVE on every one of the 24 tensors, worst
absolute 4.65e-04 on enc.block.8.out. That is float accumulation order
only. The graph — the in-block stride-2 subsampling with its mean-pooled
and trimmed residual, the Shaw bias index sign, the self-conditioned CTC
injection after block 7, and the tied CTC head — is therefore exact, and
the budgets below are absorbing storage dtype, not an unlocated bug.
Widened vs the Stage 2 magnitude budget (1e-4 x p99_abs / 1e-5 x rms):
every encoder tensor, by 24x to 242x, for the reason above. The widening
is largest where the residual stream is at its widest (block 1's
post_conv / post_ff2, right after the second subsampling) and smallest on
enc.ctc.mid_injection, whose input is a softmax and therefore bounded.
NOT widened: mel.in keeps its Stage 2 magnitude budget (1.482e-04). The
C++ frontend sits 5x inside it at 1.824e-05 (1.2e-05 relative), identical
on the BF16 and F32 builds because the frontend is host F32 code that
never touches a weight. Tightening it to the observed value was not done
without user sign-off, per the Stage 4 recipe.
Downstream check that these budgets do not hide an accuracy loss: the
BF16 C++ transcript is character-identical to the reference on both dump
cases, and the full LibriSpeech test-clean gate is in the family doc.
Re-finalized entry, depthwise-conv change (post-Stage-4 perf work):
enc.ctc_logits max_abs 0.0922 -> 0.227. The granite5_ctc conv module moved
from conformer::conv_2d_dw_f32 (im2col + mul_mat) to
conformer::conv_2d_dw_direct_f32 for speed (M4/Metal/F32 encoder
114.7 ms -> 101.4 ms). The two accumulate differently, and on the dots
case that moved this tensor's max_abs from 6.150e-02 to 1.513e-01,
past the old 1.5x-observed budget.
This was localized before it was absorbed, not widened on the drift
number alone:
1. F32 replay. Against an F32-tier GGUF and the F32 oracle, the
direct build matches on BOTH cases at the same 1e-5-relative level
the im2col build does, and on this very tensor it is marginally
So the graph stays exact; only the BF16 rounding pattern moved.
2. mean_abs IMPROVED in the same run (5.442e-03 vs 5.504e-03), and it
is mean_abs, not max_abs, that tracks accuracy here. max_abs on
this tensor is a 1-in-7.2M order statistic (441 x 16384), which a
change of rounding pattern moves freely at fixed accuracy.
3. Accuracy held end to end: full LibriSpeech test-clean is 1.33% at
batch 1 and batch 8 with the identical 527 sub / 87 del / 92 ins
split, and all 2620 hypotheses are BYTE-IDENTICAL to the im2col
baseline. Batch text parity against the frozen golden and bit-exact
(0.0) batch tensor parity both still hold.
No other entry moved; every other tensor stayed inside its budget.
